text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Communist Akel had proposed to the centre-right Democratic Party that former finance minister Christos Mavrellis be fielded as the opposition's candidate in the presidential poll due next year.
- Cyprus Airways chairman Takis Kyriakides warns the company could go bust by 1999 if no new investments are made.
- Former president George Vassiliou urges the government to adopt a more positive approach in the upcoming intercommunal talks with the Turkish side on the Cyprus conflict.
- Drastic action is needed to save Cyprus Airways, says its chairman.
- Cyprus Airways moot over enforcing an early retirement scheme for 500 employees, selling planes and dropping loss-making routes.
- Communist Akel makes a proposal to the Democratic Party on cooperating in the upcoming presidential elections.
- Argentine President Carlos Menem will come to Cyprus on Wednesday.
- Akel has suggested Christos Mavrellis be the opposition's candidate in the presidential elections.
- The Turkish occupation army in northern Cyprus has upgraded its capabilities.
- Cypriots regularly beat their wives, says domestic violence centre.
- Cyprus Airways faces bankruptcy by 1999 if there is a deregulation of flights.
- Eleni Foka, the Greek Cypriot teacher in Turkish-held Karpasia, comes for medical treatment.
